verdict.summary: Registering a GitHub OAuth app is self-serve and has no documented review for public use. The friction comes from organization OAuth app access restrictions, rate limits and token limits. Review applies only to optional Marketplace listings.
verdict.approval_wait: none (Marketplace listing only: about 2-6 weeks, community-reported)

gates.name: Your own account (unreviewed OAuth app)
gates.unlocks: Register the app and connect your own GitHub account right away.
limits: Private or enterprise-managed apps only allow sign-in by members of the owning org or enterprise
Orgs with OAuth app access restrictions block unapproved apps from private org resources until an owner approves

gates.name: Other users (no formal test mode)
gates.unlocks: Any GitHub user can authorize the app. No test-user allowlist is documented. Org resources need per-org approval.
limits: Ten tokens per user/app/scope combination; ten new tokens per hour, then a re-authorization prompt
Org approval is per organization; owners control who can request it
No documented user or install cap (not verified)
gates.time_to_reach: Immediate; org approvals depend on each org owner

gates.name: Public / Marketplace listing
gates.unlocks: Optional GitHub Marketplace listing for discovery. It is not needed for public use of the OAuth app.
limits: Paid plans need a verified-publisher org and at least 200 users for OAuth apps
Free listings have no user minimum
Per-app limit of 2,000 token requests per hour; increases are granted per app

steps.title: Sign in and choose an owner
steps.detail: Sign in to GitHub. Decide whether the app is owned by your personal account or by an organization. An org suits team maintenance, and ownership can be transferred later.

steps.title: Copy the callback URL from Composio
steps.detail: Create a GitHub auth config in Composio and copy the callback URL it shows. Confirm it there, because Composio's listed default redirect differs from the one seen in probing.
gotchas: Do not assume the older v1 redirect is correct.

steps.title: Register the OAuth app
steps.detail: Go to Settings > Developer settings > OAuth Apps > New OAuth App (github.com/settings/applications/new). Fill in the app name, homepage URL and description, and paste the callback URL. The exact form fields were not verified against the primary page.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: Apps can register up to 10 callback URIs. Wildcard matching is set per URI.
For local testing use the literal 127.0.0.1, not localhost.

steps.title: Generate the client secret and enter credentials in Composio
steps.detail: On the app page, copy the Client ID and generate a client secret. Paste both into the Composio auth config.

steps.title: Choose narrow scopes
steps.detail: Pick the minimum scopes instead of Composio's broad default (repo, user, gist, notifications, project, workflow, codespace). Add user:email if you need the email address. Scopes are sent space-delimited, and users can reduce them at consent.

values.label: Scopes
values.value: e.g. read:user user:email (add repo only if needed)

steps.title: Decide on token expiry and PKCE
steps.detail: Optionally enable expiring tokens, which last 8 hours with a 6-month refresh token, or request offline_access per sign-in. PKCE supports S256 only. Enable device flow in the app settings if you need headless use.
gotchas: Enabling the app-wide setting does not expire tokens already issued.

steps.title: Connect your own account
steps.detail: Run the Composio authorization with your GitHub account and check that the token works. An unknown client_id just shows a login page, so a login wall does not by itself mean the app is misconfigured.

steps.title: Get organization approval where needed
steps.detail: For users in orgs with OAuth app access restrictions, they request approval and an org owner approves your app. Do this per org. Tell customers' admins to expect it.
gotchas: Restricted orgs give an unapproved app no access to private resources.
Restrictions are on by default for new orgs.

steps.title: Plan for token and rate limits
steps.detail: Reuse tokens instead of re-authorizing. Stay under ten tokens per user/app/scope and 2,000 token requests per hour. User API calls count against each user's 5,000 per hour. GitHub recommends GitHub Apps for new integrations at scale.

steps.title: Optional: list on GitHub Marketplace
steps.detail: Only needed for a Marketplace listing. Prepare a privacy policy, support contact, logo and screenshots, and accept the Developer Agreement. For paid plans, transfer the app to an org and complete publisher verification.

steps.title: Submit the listing and wait
steps.detail: Click Submit for review in the draft listing. An onboarding expert contacts you. Community reports suggest about 2-6 weeks.

requirements.detail: The developer settings page requires sign-in.
The redirect host and port must match the registered callback, and the path must sit under the registered path.

requirements.item: Org owner approval for restricted orgs
requirements.detail: Needed per organization with OAuth app access restrictions.

requirements.item: Verified publisher org, privacy policy, support contact, assets
requirements.detail: Marketplace listing requirements. Paid plans also need an org owner and, for OAuth apps, 200 users.

scopes.effect: High privilege, in Composio's defaults. No documented review gate, but users see it on the consent screen.
High privilege, in Composio's defaults. Not review-gated in the docs.
Fully manages the org. Not review-gated, but orgs may refuse approval.
Needed to read the user's email for sign-in.
Narrow read scope for profile data.

blockers.symptom: Members cannot authorize the app for org resources, or get no private org data
blockers.cause: The org has OAuth app access restrictions and your app is unapproved.
blockers.fix: Ask an org owner to approve the app. Owners can also change who may request approval.

blockers.symptom: New token generation blocked or outages
blockers.cause: Over 2,000 access-token requests per hour for the app.
blockers.fix: Cache and refresh tokens, reduce re-authorizations, or consider a GitHub App. Rate-limit increases are granted per app.

blockers.symptom: Re-authorization prompt, or older tokens stop working
blockers.cause: More than ten tokens per user/app/scope, or ten tokens or sign-ins in an hour.
blockers.fix: Reuse existing tokens instead of minting new ones.

blockers.cause: GitHub publishes no openid-configuration at that path.
blockers.fix: Configure the authorize and token endpoints manually.

blockers.cause: Only the S256 method is supported.
blockers.fix: Use S256 and send the code_verifier on token exchange.

composio.note: Start on Composio's managed GitHub app to test quickly. Register your own app when you need your own client ID/secret, callback URL, narrower scopes (the defaults include repo and workflow), or your own branding and rate limits. Confirm the callback URL in your Composio auth config before registering.

evidence.claim: Composio lists a managed OAuth2 config for GitHub with broad default scopes.
evidence.quote: managed_oauth_available: true; default_scopes: repo, user, gist, notifications, project, workflow, codespace

evidence.claim: OAuth apps can register up to 10 callback URIs with per-URI wildcard setting.
evidence.quote: OAuth apps can now register up to 10 redirect URIs (called callback URIs on GitHub)

evidence.claim: Redirect host and port must match the callback; path must be under it.
evidence.quote: the redirect URL's host (excluding sub-domains) and port must exactly match the callback URL

evidence.claim: Use loopback literal 127.0.0.1 rather than localhost.
evidence.quote: OAuth RFC recommends not to use localhost, but instead to use loopback literal 127.0.0.1 or IPv6 ::1.

evidence.claim: PKCE supports S256 only.
evidence.quote: Must be S256 - the plain code challenge method is not supported.

evidence.claim: Device flow must be enabled in app settings.
evidence.quote: you must first enable it in your app's settings

evidence.claim: Users can reduce granted scopes.
evidence.quote: users can edit their scopes, effectively granting your application less access than you originally requested.

evidence.claim: Scope catalogue includes high-privilege scopes; none labeled as review-gated.
evidence.quote: admin:org: Fully manage the organization and its teams, projects, and memberships.

evidence.claim: user:email is needed to read the user's email.
evidence.quote: Be sure to at least enable the user:email scope, as this is required to retrieve the user's email address

evidence.claim: Requested scopes are normalized to drop implied ones.
evidence.quote: discarding those that are implicitly included by another requested scope

evidence.claim: 2,000 access token requests per hour per OAuth app.
evidence.quote: OAuth apps are subject to a rate limit of 2,000 access token requests per hour.

evidence.claim: The authorize endpoint redirects an unknown client_id to a sign-in page.
evidence.quote: final_url: github.com/login?client_id=oauth-runway-probe-invalid-client

evidence.claim: User OAuth calls count against the user's 5,000 per hour limit.
evidence.quote: All of these requests count towards your personal rate limit of 5,000 requests per hour.

evidence.claim: Rate-limit increases are per OAuth app.
evidence.quote: Rate limit increases are granted per OAuth app.

evidence.claim: OAuth apps have lower rate limits and GitHub Apps are recommended.
evidence.quote: OAuth apps have lower rate limits and do not scale.

evidence.claim: Org OAuth app access restrictions block unapproved apps; on by default for new orgs.
evidence.quote: organization members and outside collaborators cannot authorize OAuth app access to organization resources.

evidence.claim: Unapproved apps get no private org API access.
evidence.quote: API access to private organization resources is not available for unapproved OAuth apps.

evidence.claim: Org owners control who can request app approval.
evidence.quote: Members only: Block outside collaborators from requesting apps while permitting organization members to do so.

evidence.claim: OAuth app access requests are per-org approvals.
evidence.quote: For OAuth apps this is a request to allow the app through the About OAuth app access restrictions

evidence.claim: Private/enterprise OAuth apps limit sign-in to owning org/enterprise members.
evidence.quote: to sign into an app, users must now be a member of the enterprise if it is internal, or the owning organization if it's private.

evidence.claim: Ten tokens per user/app/scope and ten new tokens per hour.
evidence.quote: There is a limit of ten tokens that are issued per user/application/scope combination, and a rate limit of ten tokens created per hour.

evidence.claim: Ten sign-ins per hour then re-authorization, separate from token limit.
evidence.quote: This ten sign in rate limit is distinct from the ten token limit also enforced for OAuth apps.

evidence.claim: Developer settings sits behind a sign-in wall.
evidence.quote: login_wall: true; title: Sign in to GitHub

evidence.claim: No documented install/user cap or test mode for unreviewed OAuth apps was found.
Marketplace listings need a privacy policy, contact, support, and more.
evidence.quote: Listings must have a valid link to a privacy policy.

evidence.claim: Listings need logo, feature card, screenshots, webhooks, and the Developer Agreement.
evidence.quote: Apps must have a logo, feature card, and screenshots images that meet the recommendations

evidence.claim: Paid plans need a verified-publisher org owner.
evidence.quote: your app must be owned by an organization that is a verified publisher.

evidence.claim: Paid OAuth apps need 200 users; free has no minimum.
evidence.quote: OAuth apps should have a minimum of 200 users.

evidence.claim: Publisher verification is requested by an org owner and reviewed by GitHub.
evidence.quote: Click Request Verification. GitHub will review your details and let you know once your publisher verification is complete.

evidence.claim: Listing is submitted for review; Marketplace section needs any-user installability.
evidence.quote: The Marketplace section is only visible if you allowed your app to be installed by any user or organization when registering the app.

evidence.claim: Community reports Marketplace review of 2-6 weeks.

evidence.claim: Personal-account apps must be transferred to an org before selling.
evidence.quote: If you want to sell an app that's owned by your personal account, first you'll need to transfer the app to an organization

evidence.quote: The client ID you received from GitHub when you registered. (links to github.com/settings/applications/new)

evidence.claim: Apps are created under Developer settings > OAuth Apps, or under an organization.

open_questions: The OAuth app registration form fields were not verified against the primary creating-an-OAuth-app page.
No install cap, user cap or test-mode limit was found for unreviewed OAuth apps. Check the changelog for newer changes.
No scope is documented as review-gated; only org-level approval gates access.
The 2-6 week Marketplace review time is a community figure, not an SLA.
Confirm which callback URL Composio expects, since its listed default differs from the one seen in probing.
Whether GitHub will raise the 2,000 token-request limit for a specific app is not documented.
